graph.title: Raid VPR (5981-1)
notes: Steps are pictures only; exact stud-to-stud contacts are inferred from the images. Pieces that connect to several others have numbered stud ports so no port is used twice. Which numbered stud meets which piece is arbitrary.
Ids b1..b68 follow build order (steps 1-21), then the police minifig b58-b63 and the alien minifig b64-b68 from page 2.
Step 3: the box lists a white hull piece (4261693) and a dark grey inverted slope (4211064); the arrows show only the grey slope being placed. I assumed the hull is added on top of the step-2 slope.
Step 5: the placement of the two white wedges (4160325, 4160343) is inferred.
Steps 7 and 8 are two mirrored Technic sub-assemblies. I wrote them out as separate parts, not as a repeat.

In step 12 each wing (4558797, 4558802) is assumed to fit onto the black pin (4121715) of one of the step 7 / step 8 assemblies. The blue long pins already pass through the grey brick and the white brick, so I did not give them a second join to the wings.
Stickers (police logos, panel stickers) have no element ID and are not modelled.

Part 4520320 is in the catalogue as a tipper bucket, but the booklet shows a grey rod with an end stud (step 20). I used the catalogue id anyway. The rod passes through the hole of 4562148, so that join has no port on the rod.
The canopy (step 21) attachment points are inferred.
The jetpack (b61) goes round the police minifig's neck, but the catalogue torso 4551188 has only one 'neck' port and it is already used by the head, so that join has no port on the torso side.

The 3 separate groups are real and intended, so I kept them. The booklet builds three things: the spaceship (b1-b57), the police astronaut minifig (b58-b63, page 2) and the alien minifig (b64-b68, page 2). The booklet never attaches either minifig to the ship. Page 19 shows both standing next to the ship. The pilot-in-cockpit pose appears only on the cover. A join between them would be invented.
Pages after 20 are adverts and are not part of the build.

graph_initial.title: Raid VPR (5981-1)
notes: Steps are pictures only; exact stud-to-stud contacts are inferred from the images, so which stud port connects to which piece is approximate. Most multi-stud pieces use a single stud.1 / anti-stud.1 port.
Ids b1..b68 follow build order (steps 1-21, then the police minifig b58-b63 and the alien minifig b64-b68 from page 2).
Step 3: the box lists a white hull piece (4261693) and a dark grey inverted slope (4211064); the arrows show only the grey slope being placed. I assumed the hull is added on top of the step-2 slope.
Step 5: the placement of the two white wedges (4160325, 4160343) is inferred (one on the hull, one on the grey slope and the first wedge).
Steps 7 and 8 are two mirrored Technic sub-assemblies (grey 1x1 Technic brick + blue long pin + white 1x2 brick + black pin with axle hole). I wrote them out as separate parts, not as a repeat.
In step 12 the two wings (4558797, 4558802) are assumed to fit onto the pins of the step 7 and step 8 assemblies, one wing on each assembly.
Stickers (police logos, panel stickers on the 1x2 tile, tail fin and wings) have no element ID and are not modelled.

Part 4520320 is in the catalogue as a tipper bucket, but the booklet shows a grey rod with an end stud (step 20). I used the catalogue id anyway. The rod passes through the hole of 4562148, so that join has no port on the rod.
The canopy (step 21) attachment points are inferred.
Page 21 and the pages after it are adverts (set 5982 and others) and are not part of the build.

final_issue_list: the build is 3 separate groups of pieces; connect them unless the booklet really builds separate models
